## `octeliumctl`

```text
Manage Cluster resources

Usage:
  octeliumctl [command]

Available Commands:
  apply       Apply the desired state to the Cluster
  auth        Authentication-related operations to the Cluster
  create      Create a Cluster resource
  delete      Delete a Cluster resource
  get         List or get Cluster resources
  login       Log in to a Cluster
  logout      Log out from a Cluster
  update      Update a Cluster resource
  version     Print version information

Flags:
      --domain string    The Cluster Domain
      --homedir string   Override Octelium home directory
      --logout           Log out after executing the command. This is useful when using commands such as "octelium connect" inside ephemeral environments such as containers
```

## `octeliumctl apply`

```text
Declaratively apply the desired state to the Cluster. This command
accepts both single yaml files and directories. For the case of directories, all yaml files and sub-directories will be recursively searched for resources.

Usage:
  octeliumctl apply [FILE_OR_DIRECTORY]... [flags]

Examples:

# Apply changes from a single file
octeliumctl apply /path/to/file.yaml

# Apply changes from a root directory, all yaml files and sub-directories are automatically included
octeliumctl apply /path/to/directory

# Apply changes from multiple files and directories at once
octeliumctl apply /path/to/file.yaml /path/to/directory

# Apply from stdin
cat /path/to/file.yaml | octeliumctl apply -

# Only include changes in User and Group types
octeliumctl apply --include User --include Group /path/to/file.yaml

# Exclude changes in Services
octeliumctl apply --exclude Service /path/to/file.yaml

# Include Secrets in addition to the default Resource kinds
octeliumctl apply --include-secret /path/to/directory

# Synchronize the Cluster to the desired state and delete the Resources that are not described in it
octeliumctl apply --prune /path/to/directory

Flags:
      --exclude strings   Exclude these Resource kinds from the list of included kinds.
                          Use the flag multiple times to exclude more kinds
      --include strings   Only include these Resource kinds. This overrides the default list of included kinds.
                          Use the flag multiple times to include more kinds
      --include-secret    Include Secret Resources. This by default is disabled in order to not encourage defining your Secrets inside configs that are meant to be stored in git repos for example
      --prune             Delete the Resources that exist in the Cluster but are not described in the desired state.
                          This synchronizes the Cluster to the described state instead of only creating and updating Resources. Disabled by default
```

## `octeliumctl create config`

```text
Create a Config

Usage:
  octeliumctl create config [flags]

Aliases:
  config, cfg, conf, configs

Examples:

octeliumctl create config my-config
octeliumctl create config --file /path/to/config/file my-cfg-1
octeliumctl create config -f /path/to/config/file my-cfg-1
octeliumctl create config --value SOME_VALUE cfg-02
octeliumctl create config my-config --from-env MY_VALUE
echo $MY_VALUE | octeliumctl create config my-config --file -

Flags:
  -f, --file -            Get Config value from file path. Set it to - to read from stdin
      --from-env string   Get Config value from an environment variable
      --value string      Config value
```

## `octeliumctl create credential`

```text
Create a Credential

Usage:
  octeliumctl create credential [flags]

Aliases:
  credential, cred, creds, credentials

Examples:

octeliumctl create credential --user usr1 my-cred
octeliumctl create cred --user usr1 --expire-in 3months my-cred
octeliumctl create credential --user usr2 --expire-in 15minutes --one-time
octeliumctl create cred --user usr3 --expire-in 30days
octeliumctl create cred --user usr4 --type access-token --policy my-policy
octeliumctl create cred --user usr5 --type oauth2 --session-type clientless
octeliumctl create cred --user usr6 -o json
octeliumctl create cred --rotate my-cred

Flags:
      --expire-in 2hours      Set the duration after which the Credential expires (e.g. 2hours, `30days`, `6hours`, `1week`)
      --max-authn uint32      Maximum number of authentications. Overrides one-time if set
      --one-time              Use this Credential only once for authentication and then delete it
  -o, --out string            Output format (json|yaml)
      --policy strings        Policy attached to Sessions created by this Credential. Use the flag multiple times to add more Policies.
      --rotate                Generate new token for an already created Credential (i.e. rotate the Credential)
      --session-type string   Session type (Can take the values: "client" or "clientless"). By default it is set to "client"
      --type string           Credential type (Can take the values: "auth-token", "access-token" or "oauth2"). By default it is set to "auth-token"
      --user string           User name
```

## `octeliumctl create secret`

```text
Create a Secret

Usage:
  octeliumctl create secret [flags]

Aliases:
  secret, sec, secrets

Examples:

octeliumctl create secret my-api-token
octeliumctl create secret -f /path/to/secret/file secret1
octeliumctl create secret --file ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 ssh-key
octeliumctl create secret --value TOP_SECRET secret2
octeliumctl create secret my-secret --from-env MY_SECRET
echo $MY_SECRET | octeliumctl create secret my-secret --file -
octeliumctl create secret mtls-k8s-01 --cert /PATH/TO/CERTIFICATE_CHAIN.PEM --cert-key /PATH/TO/CERTIFICATE_PRIVATE_KEY.PEM

Flags:
      --cert string       Certificate file path. This automatically sets --type to "cert"
      --cert-key string   Certificate private key file path. This automatically sets --type to "cert"
  -f, --file -            Get Secret value from file path. Set it to - to read from stdin
      --from-env string   Get Secret value from an environment variable
      --type string       Secret type (Can take the values: "value" or "cert"). By default it is set to "value" (default "value")
      --value string      Secret value
```

## `octeliumctl login`

```text
Log in to a Cluster

Usage:
  octeliumctl login [flags]

Examples:

octeliumctl login --auth-token <AUTHENTICATION_TOKEN>
octeliumctl login --domain octelium.example.com

Flags:
      --assertion string    Authenticate using an assertion. Refer to the docs for more details.
      --auth-token string   Authentication Token
      --scope strings
                            Scope is a way to limit the access to certain Services and Octelium APIs that works similarly to OAuth2.
                            This flag is used ONLY while authenticating using the --auth-token or --assertion flags.
                            You can use this flag also using the login subcommand.
                            For example, you can only limit the Session to access the Service "svc1.ns1" only using the scope "service:svc1.ns1"
                            You can also limit yourself to access only Services belonging to the Namespace "ns2" using the scope "service:ns2/*"
                            You can also use multiple scopes in the same command as follows "--scope service:svc1 --scope service:ns3/*"

      --web                 Authenticate using the web Portal
```

## `octeliumctl update credential`

```text
  octeliumctl update device [flags]

Aliases:
  device, dev, devices

Examples:

 octeliumctl update device --approve usr1-linux-uvc4
 octeliumctl update dev --reject usr1-linux-uvc4

Flags:
      --approve   Approve the Device
      --reject    Reject the Device
```

## `octeliumctl update secret`

```text
Update a Secret

Usage:
  octeliumctl update secret [flags]

Aliases:
  secret, sec, secrets

Examples:

octeliumctl update secret my-api-token
octeliumctl update secret -f /path/to/secret/file secret1
octeliumctl update secret --file ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 ssh-key
octeliumctl update secret --value TOP_SECRET secret2
octeliumctl update secret my-secret --from-env MY_SECRET
echo $MY_SECRET | octeliumctl update secret my-secret --file -
octeliumctl update secret mtls-k8s-01 --cert /PATH/TO/CERTIFICATE_CHAIN.PEM --cert-key /PATH/TO/CERTIFICATE_PRIVATE_KEY.PEM

Flags:
      --cert string       Certificate file path. This automatically sets --type to "cert"
      --cert-key string   Certificate private key file path. This automatically sets --type to "cert"
  -f, --file -            Get Secret value from file path. Set it to - to read from stdin
      --from-env string   Get Secret value from an environment variable
      --type string       Secret type (Can take the values: "value" or "cert"). By default it is set to "value" (default "value")
      --value string      Secret value
```

## `octeliumctl update session`

```text
Update a Session

Usage:
  octeliumctl update session [flags]

Aliases:
  session, sess, sessions

Examples:

  octeliumctl update session --expire-in 3months usr1-0vgiqs75psre
  octeliumctl update sess --approve usr1-0vgiqs75psre
  octeliumctl update sess --reject usr1-0vgiqs75psre

Flags:
      --approve            Approve the Session
      --expire-in 2hours   Set the duration after which the Session expires (e.g. 2hours, `30days`, `6hours`, `1week`)
      --reject             Reject the Session
```

## `octeliumctl version`

```text
Print version information

Usage:
  octeliumctl version [flags]

Flags:
      --check        Check whether there is a more recent latest release for Octelium CLIs
  -o, --out string   Output format (json|yaml) (default "yaml")
```
